source_name: eBIZ, s.r.o. – operator of eZakazky / eTrhovisko
why_relevant: Vendor site describing the eZakazky product line and its customer base; route to enumerating buyer sub-portals and understanding what data each module (DNS, e-auction, eTrhovisko) exposes.

source_name: TENDERnet – prieskum trhu / nízke hodnoty
why_relevant: Platform for market surveys and low-value contracts (§117) with individually addressable public calls (/vyzva/{token}). Captures the sub-threshold layer — small IT, terminal, cash-handling and service purchases — that is absent from the ÚVO Vestník.

source_name: Verejnazakazka.sk – bezplatný monitoring (obstaravanie.verejnazakazka.sk)
why_relevant: Free daily email monitoring that crawls hundreds of buyer websites (municipalities, schools, hospitals, companies) — i.e. it reaches buyer-site postings that never hit a central platform. Zero-cost baseline feed.

source_name: ADVAL monitoring verejného obstarávania
why_relevant: Entity-centric monitoring: alerts when a *watched buyer* publishes anything new. Ideal for standing watch on a named list of banks, insurers and payment-sector buyers rather than keyword sweeps.

source_name: eTENDERs.sk
why_relevant: Additional Slovak tender aggregation/monitoring portal surfaced alongside the main players; worth profiling for coverage of non-state buyers.

source_name: Tender.sk – Slovensko (štátne aj súkromné zákazky)
why_relevant: Explicitly markets coverage of both state and PRIVATE contracts in Slovakia — directly on-cell for the private-buyer bypass route.

source_name: VOKO.sk – portál o verejnom obstarávaní
why_relevant: Portal offering a lifecycle view of contracts and monitoring tools; useful for tracking a tender from announcement through award and for cross-checking platform-hosted competitions.

source_name: eGov-Obstarávania (obstaravania.egov.sk)
why_relevant: Third-party commercial publication service hosting buyer profiles for municipalities, schools and legal entities that embed it on their own websites — a bypass channel distinct from ÚVO and from the big e-sourcing platforms.

source_name: VÚB banka – Nákup a obstarávanie (supplier page)
why_relevant: A private commercial bank's own procurement/supplier page — the canonical bypass route: sourcing rules and vendor onboarding published by the bank, not by any state portal. Likely names the e-sourcing tool the Intesa group uses in SK.

source_name: Národná banka Slovenska – verejné súťaže / profil obstarávateľa
why_relevant: NBS states it runs above-threshold procurement through IS JOSEPHINE, and separately publishes selected commercial competitions plus orders/contracts/invoices. Confirms the platform route for the sector's most important SK buyer and anchors buyer-name matching on JOSEPHINE.

source_name: Transparency International Slovensko – monitoring verejného obstarávania
why_relevant: Watchdog methodology and datasets on Slovak procurement; useful for judging platform data quality, identifying systematic non-publication, and for red-flag heuristics applied to platform-hosted competitions.

source_name: obstaravame.sk (PHZ Tender) – procurement consultancy
why_relevant: Consultancy that runs competitions on behalf of buyers (often via TENDERnet/JOSEPHINE); its client and case-study pages reveal buyers and upcoming purchases before formal publication.

source_name: Vestník verejného obstarávania (ÚVO – Úrad pre verejné obstarávanie)
why_relevant: Statutory Slovak procurement bulletin: every above/below-threshold notice, including ATM servicing, cash-in-transit, kiosk and payment-terminal contracts, must be published here on business days via the eForms system. This is the canonical primary feed for payments-infrastructure tenders and award notices in SK.

source_name: JOSEPHINE (PROEBIZ) – e-procurement platform, public tender list
why_relevant: Roughly a fifth of Slovak procurement notices run through JOSEPHINE, and crucially the tender documentation (technical specifications for terminals, kiosks, gateways) is hosted here rather than in the bulletin. A search hit already surfaced a payment-card functional specification annex hosted on this platform.

source_name: ERANET – e-procurement platform family (multi-instance)
why_relevant: ERANET carries roughly a tenth of Slovak notices and is deployed as dozens of per-buyer instances (subdomain-per-customer). Enumerating instances is the only way to reach several state-owned buyers' tender documentation directly.

source_name: NBS – SEPA instant credit transfer / payments pages
why_relevant: Regulatory timetable and national implementation plan for SEPA instant payments in SK (reachability Jan 2025, sending Oct 2025, verification-of-payee). Deadlines of this kind are the direct upstream cause of bank-side integration procurements, so this page dates and explains gateway/instant-payment tender waves.

source_name: Slovenská banková asociácia (SBA) – projects and card statistics
source_subtype: industry association / project and statistics publisher
why_relevant: The banking association co-authors the national instant-payments plan with NBS, MF SR and Štátna pokladnica, and publishes card issuing/acceptance statistics. It signals sector-wide programmes (verification of payee, instant payments rollout) months before individual bank procurements surface, and its statistics size the card/terminal estate.

source_name: Ministerstvo financií SR – press releases on euro cash transport arrangements
why_relevant: MF SR has publicly communicated on securing euro cash transport within Slovakia — state-level CIT arrangements that sit upstream of, and sometimes replace, competitive CIT tenders. Press releases date and frame these decisions.

source_name: Loomis Slovakia – ATM management, cash transport and cash processing services
why_relevant: Supply-side mirror of the demand landscape: the dominant CIT/ATM-outsourcing incumbent in SK, describing exactly which services banks outsource (ATM management, cash logistics, service management) and confirming that cash processing runs under an NBS licence. Its service catalogue is the practical vocabulary that tender scopes are written in.

source_name: Monilogi s.r.o. – cash processing and ATM replenishment provider (SK)
why_relevant: Second-tier SK cash-handling actor doing cash preparation and distribution for bank branches, corporate clients and ATM networks via certified CIT partners — evidence that the SK CIT/ATM-servicing market has more than one credible bidder, and a name to watch in award notices.

source_name: ProtectUs (súkromná bezpečnostná služba) – cash and valuables transport, ATM provisioning
why_relevant: SBS-licensed operator listing cash/valuables transport, sorting and counting, banknote authenticity verification, ATM provisioning and FX processing — shows that in SK the CIT bidder pool overlaps with the private security (SBS) sector, which matters for how CIT tenders are worded and which CPV codes they use.

source_name: Dopravný podnik Bratislava (DPB) – ticket vending machine estate and modernisation
why_relevant: Public transport operators are a major non-bank buyer of self-service kiosks with card acceptance. DPB is modernising its vending machine network and has stated an intent to roughly double card-accepting machines by end-2026 — a concrete, dated pipeline signal for kiosk and terminal vendors, whose procurement will land in ÚVO/JOSEPHINE.

source_name: Obchodný vestník (Ministry of Justice commercial gazette)
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly source: corporate events of payments-infrastructure suppliers (mergers, liquidations, insolvency, capital changes of CIT firms, ATM deployers, terminal distributors) that reshape the bidder pool but never appear in procurement feeds.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe – Referencie (client reference list, SK)
why_relevant: Asseco CE is the dominant Slovak core-banking/card-processing supplier (eStarBANK, Security Server, omnichannel). Its reference list names bank customers that never publish supplier identities themselves, so it maps otherwise-hidden private-bank sourcing relationships and is a snowball source for further actor names.
